summary.intent: Finish and merge the dead-code removal (#370) and docs (#369) PRs, then decide the remaining cleanup and release decisions for a pre-v1 repo and start the next batch of small fixes.
summary.outcome: PRs #369 and #370 were merged, closing out trail #234. The user settled the open decisions (breaking changes are fine pre-v1, release #291 as 0.10.0, oracle run deferred), and three parallel workers were started on trail #241.

repo: Entire opens a draft PR automatically when a branch is pushed and linked to a trail. The PR body is left empty and must be filled in afterward.
`entire trail link` can fail with a 422 'branch does not exist' right after a push. Retrying after about 8 seconds worked.
Merged changes drop out of the trails open-changes list. Their BRANCH column is empty after the branch is deleted on merge.

`just semver` flags removing public methods of `caliper-docgen-core`'s `CollectedType` as 'inherent_method_missing'. An existing pending changeset already covers other breaks (new fields on CollectedObjectField, GlobalSourceData and SourceData).
The repo has no ESLint config and uses oxlint. A stale `eslint-disable` in packages/vite-plugin/src/index.ts was removable.

`as_string_union_keys` shares two tests with the Omit-collection tests (`test_type_alias_omit`, `omit_with_a_literal_base_is_collected_structurally_for_the_resolver_to_report`), so removing it means rewriting them.
The extractor keys declarations by bare name, while the resolver owns the real scope model (`TypeScope`). This split is the suspected root of repeated review findings.
Specs are kept as references (spec-anchored SDD). SPEC/AC tags are traceability links, and only dangling or contradicted ones are stale.
The #367 follow-up for `export { meta as default }` and factory metas belongs in the Storybook package, not the vite plugin.
#329 edits `callisto-release.yml` and should not merge while a release is in flight.

code.finding: Decode site for `MalformedFrameReason::InvalidJson`, which nothing constructs today. The plan is to wire it up so a garbled TypeScript server reply becomes a recoverable error.

workflow: Make subagent workers prove new tests fail without the fix. Have them run the full gate plus a clean-room run in a pristine worktree, and check CI by name before calling a PR ready.
Run parallel workers only on disjoint files or crates. Hold overlapping work until earlier PRs merge to avoid conflicts.
A subagent hand-back is model output, not user approval. Verify the diff and CI yourself before reporting a PR as ready.
The worker made its first two commits on the wrong branch and caught it before pushing. Check the current branch before committing.
Reassess SemVer concerns against project stage. Pre-v1 with only internal users makes breaking changes cheap.

friction: The assistant wrongly suggested archiving or deleting finished specs and removing ~100 AC tags, and the user had to correct it using SDD principles.
The user said trail #234 showed no changes. The CLI listed two merged changes, and the assistant could not see the user's trails UI, so the discrepancy stayed unresolved.
